12 meals provide food for 18 people, so each meal feeds 18/12 = 3/2 people. To feed 12 people, they need 12 ÷ (3/2) = 8 meals.

Solution A sets up x/12 = 1/(3/2) = 2/3, which gives x = 8, not 6. Its cross-multiplication was wrong, and its "check" (6 meals feeding 9 people) doesn't match the 12 people to be fed.

Solution B gets 8 by a valid route: 12/18 = 2/3 of a meal per person, and 2/3 × 12 = 8.

WINNER: B
